newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan CPC oil refinery in small fire.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan CPC oil refinery in small fire.

text.p: Taiwan's state monopoly Chinese Petroleum Corp said on Monday that a small fire broke out in part of its southern oil refinery plant on Saturday, causing its temporary closure, but production would resume in that section of the plant within two or three days.

"A small fire occurred in our Kaohsiung oil refinery plant's residual cracking system on Saturday night. After extinguishing the fire within 40 minutes, we found a screw loose problem had caused the fire," the firm's spokeswoman Ho Li-chun said by telephone.
"It's nothing serious, and we should resume production of this part within two or three days after the Kaohsiung City Government's investigation and approval to resume operations," she said.
Ho added the temporary closure of the residual cracking system would not affect the overall oil refinery.
She said the company had yet to calculate the cost of any loss from the fire, but it would be very small. The local China Times newspaper on Monday estimated the loss at around T$500,000.
